title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises to adopt new business models, technology and techniques to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: Local governments in Bosnia and Herzegovina are able to work with the social partners and other local institutions to jointly identify and support start-ups by women and youth. These local employment partnerships implemented five pilot programmes together with the ILO to enhance product and business innovation and reorganization / localization of the supply chains to maintain the functioning and increase competitiveness of MSMEs. With resources made available by the Delegation of the European Commission in Bosnia and Herzegovina through a joint project with UNDP and GIZ, the ILO supported youth and women in vulnerable circumstances to access business training (SIYB) and finance in order to launch their start-ups in promising sectors (including IT). The support was delivered through local employment partnerships, which empower municipal authorities and the social partners at the local level to identify opportunities for entrepreneurship development. About 125 youth entrepreneurs were supported to launch their business through SIYB training and post-training financial support. Over 500 people (50 per cent women) received SIYB training.
